text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered -> AUTH-TRITON-3687. Elevated auth failure rate for tenant Triton Health (private VPC). Source: identity-proxy jwks fetch errors to https://idp.triton-corp.com/.well-known/jwks.json. Start=3687654321. Escalation: eng-oncall -> eng-sre -> infra.

Ivan (oncall): Acknowledged. Im starting triage. Lee please jump in. Notifying Triton SRE (Maria).

Lee (sre): On it. Can you paste the auth-bridge logs? Looking for kid mismatches or 5xx from idp.

Ivan (oncall): Snippet from auth-bridge:
```
ERROR auth.bridge: jwks fetch failed status=502 url=https://idp.triton-corp.com/.well-known/jwks.json cause="upstream 502"
WARN auth.bridge: token invalid kid="k_old" error="no matching key"
```

Bob (cust-triage): Triton reports ~35-45% failure rate on API auth for services using the private pool. Their apps are showing degraded workflows; they say no DB writes failed but some requests returned 401/503. Maria (Triton) is on call.

Amy (solutions): Do we have a tenant-level backup JWKS URL for Triton? We added caching but not a real failover earlier.

Jun (infra): Options to mitigate quickly:
- Force JWKS cache reload from control plane
- Switch tenant to a backup JWKS endpoint
- Temporarily accept legacy KIDs for the tenant (with expiry)

Jun (infra): I'll prepare commands. Will not change live routing without confirmation:
```
# inspect jwks cache
kubectl -n tenants-triton logs auth-bridge-0 --tail=200 | grep jwks
# trigger reload
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/tenants/triton/jwks/reload -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
# set backup jwks
redwoodctl tenant update triton --auth-jwks-url=https://idp-backup.triton-corp.net/.well-known/jwks.json
```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: jwks-reload-handler v1.3.2 -> triton-pool canary.

Lee (sre): I'm going to sample bearer tokens to read KIDs. If tokens still have the old KID that explains the split.

Lee (sre): Sampled KIDs from failing tokens -> ["k_7a3a","k_9c1f","k_oldb"]. Primary JWKS only returned k_9c1f prior to reload; backup contains k_7a3a.

Jun (infra): Executing reload now.

Jun (infra): POST /api/tenants/triton/jwks/reload -> 200. Auth-bridge log: JWKS cache updated; keys now [k_9c1f,k_7a3a,k_3d2e,k_oldb].

Ivan (oncall): Watching metrics. Lee, how's the auth success rate?

Lee (sre): Auth success rose from ~60% to ~90+% in 2 minutes. Some long-lived sessions still hitting old tokens and getting 401.

Maria (triton-sre): Were aware. Triton will re-issue short-lived tokens for services and perform controlled rollover. Can you add a short acceptance window for legacy keys?

Amy (solutions): We have a per-tenant flag to accept legacy KIDs for a short duration. Recommend 30 minutes while Triton completes token refresh.

Jun (infra): Applying accept_legacy_kids=true for Triton for 30m.

Jun (infra): Command executed: redwoodctl tenant patch triton --set auth.accept_legacy_kids=true --duration=30m. Control plane shows expires_at=3687656921.

Lee (sre): Post-change validation: token validation errors back to baseline. No memory spikes; JWKS cache stable. Monitoring for flapping.

Ivan (oncall): Drafting incident summary for ticket and postmortem:
- Root cause: Partial IdP signer rotation at Triton; JWKS endpoint returned rotated set before all signing endpoints rotated. Our JWKS cache and lack of backup/failover caused prolonged validation failures.
- Impact: ~40% auth failures for Triton private pool; degraded customer workflows; no data loss.
- Immediate mitigation: manual JWKS reload, enable per-tenant legacy KID acceptance, coordinate token re-issue with Triton.

Amy (solutions): Action items:
- infra/control-plane: implement automatic JWKS reload on consecutive 5xx failures + support backup JWKS URLs (owner: Jun)
- runtime: surface KID mismatch metric and per-tenant KID inventory (owner: Lee)
- customer-success: timeline and SLO assessment & customer communication (owner: Bob)

Bob (cust-triage): Maria requested an after-action meeting at 16:00 UTC. I'll schedule and prepare a short RCA and timeline. Also collecting affected routes & timestamps for SLA review.

Ivan (oncall): Handoff: Lee will monitor for 2 hours; Jun will own infra follow-up RFC (RF-2026-JWKS). I'll update the incident ticket and tag it mitigated for now.

Lee (sre): Acknowledged. Keeping dashboards pinned. If failures >5% resume, re-escalate immediately.

deploy-bot: Canary complete: jwks-reload-handler v1.3.2 rolled to triton-pool; health checks OK.

incident-bot: Incident AUTH-TRITON-3687 state=mitigated start=3687654321 mitigated=3687654478 responders=[Ivan (oncall), Lee (sre), Jun (infra), Amy (solutions), Bob (cust-triage)]

Bob (cust-triage): I'll attach logs and a customer-facing summary to the postmortem ticket. Keeping thread open for notes.
